sources.text:
Kansas man mapped rooftops near Trump speech site, threatened to shoot president: DOJ
A Kansas man allegedly vowed to shoot President Donald Trump and claimed he had already mapped rooftops near his upcoming speech, triggering a federal investigation that landed him in custody before the visit.
Jaden J. Read, 24, of Clearwater, was charged Saturday with making threats against the president, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Kansas. Authorities arrested him that same day, two days before Trump’s scheduled Monday visit to Wichita.
The investigation began Oct. 15, when a Crime Stoppers tip alerted authorities to comments beneath a KAKE News Facebook article about the president’s trip, prosecutors said.
THREE COLLEGE STUDENTS FACE FEDERAL CHARGES OVER ALLEGED THREATS AGAINST TRUMP AHEAD OF CAMPUS RALLY
“Let’s shoot Trump honestly, where’s our shooter? I’m tired of living this money life,” Read allegedly wrote.
Prosecutors said he immediately followed with another comment claiming he had ammunition and threatening to kill the president.
BUTLER MAN’S ONLINE RANTS TO KILL TRUMP END IN GUILTY PLEA AFTER FBI PROBE
Investigators then found additional alleged threats beneath a separate Facebook article from KWCH 12 News about Trump’s visit.
“Can we shoot him in Kansas please I will myself,” Read allegedly posted.
MAN ARRESTED AT TRUMP GOLF COURSE AHEAD OF PRESIDENT’S VISIT ALLEGEDLY HAD WEAPONS CACHE
A minute later, prosecutors said, he claimed to know where Trump would speak and to have studied nearby rooftops.
“IK where your speech will be. Already mapped out roofs around. Finna get kirked since yall couldn’t help him,” the comment read, according to the U.S. attorney’s office.
FLORIDA WRITE-IN CONGRESSIONAL CANDIDATE WILLIAM UPHAM ARRESTED AFTER SAYING TRUMP ‘MUST BE KILLED’
Read was taken into federal custody following his arrest in Clearwater. Prosecutors said he would remain there pending a detention hearing.
“Political violence and threats of political violence will not be tolerated,” U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser said in a statement Monday.
“The first Amendment allows for robust disagreement but there are constraints. I caution people to stay within the bounds of constitutionally protected speech.”

sources.news_title: Trump Assassination Threat: Kansas Man Accused of Mapping Out Rooftops Ahead of President's Visit, Court Docs Show
sources.text:
EXCLUSIVE: Trump Assassination Threat Horror — Kansas Man Accused of Mapping Out Rooftops Ahead of President's Visit
Oct. 19 2026, Published 7:30 p.m. ET
Donald Trump's scheduled visit to Kansas sparked a federal investigation after a 24-year-old man allegedly threatened to assassinate the commander-in-chief and claimed he had already mapped out rooftops near the president's planned appearance, RadarOnline.com can reveal.
According to federal court documents obtained by Radar, Jaden John Read was charged with threatening the president after Secret Service investigators uncovered a series of disturbing Facebook posts allegedly made just days before Trump's October 19 visit to Wichita.
Alleged Assassination Threat Before Kansas Visit
The criminal complaint, filed October 17 in the U.S. District Court for Kansas, accuses Read of making at least four threatening comments on social media, including claims that he possessed ammunition and was prepared to shoot Trump himself.
One of the most alarming messages allegedly appeared beneath a KWCH 12 News Facebook post discussing Trump's upcoming visit. "I know where your speech will be. Already mapped out roofs around," Read allegedly wrote, according to the Secret Service affidavit, which records the opening as "Ik."
The message also included a reference to being "kirked," possibly referring to the assassination of Charlie Kirk. Another comment allegedly declared: "Can we sh-- him in Kansas please I will myself."
Investigators said both comments were posted on October 15, approximately one minute apart. The affidavit does not establish whether Read actually surveyed any rooftops or possessed weapons.
Secret Service Launches Investigation
The investigation began after Wichita Police Deputy Chief Dan East contacted the Secret Service on October 15 about a Crime Stoppers tip reporting threatening Facebook comments.
According to the affidavit, the initial messages appeared beneath a KAKE News article about Trump's scheduled visit.
"Let's sh-- Trump honestly. Where's our shooter?" one comment allegedly stated.
Another claimed: "I just got a 308 and 305 round and I'm k--lling this pedo."
Secret Service Special Agent Jonathan Schmucker detailed the allegations in an affidavit supporting the criminal complaint.
Investigators subsequently identified additional threatening comments posted beneath a separate television news report.
Facebook Records Help Identify Suspect
Federal agents obtained emergency disclosure records from Facebook to identify the person behind the account.
According to the filing, investigators matched the account's registered name, birth date, telephone number, and email address with information obtained through law enforcement and state records.
Agents also traced an internet connection associated with the account to Clearwater, Kansas.
The Secret Service reported that two of the threatening comments remained publicly visible as of October 17.
Suspect Faces Five Years in Prison If Convicted
Read faces one federal count of threatening the president under Title 18, Section 871 of the United States Code. A federal magistrate judge found probable cause supporting the criminal complaint on October 17.
If convicted, Read could face up to five years in federal prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and supervised release.
The filing does not establish whether investigators recovered a firearm, uncovered an operational assassination plan, or determined that Trump faced an immediate physical threat.
The defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

sources.news_title: Man Charged With Threatening to Kill Donald Trump Ahead of Rally
sources.text:
A 24-year-old Kansas man has been arrested after allegedly urging someone to shoot President Donald Trump, officials said.
Jaden J. Read of Clearwater was arrested on Saturday, two days after authorities received a tip about a series of disturbing Facebook posts linked to Trump’s planned visit to Wichita on Monday, according to the Department of Justice.
Federal prosecutors said the investigation began on October 15, when a person contacted Crime Stoppers to report comments Read allegedly posted beneath a KAKE News story about the president’s scheduled October 19 appearance.
In one comment, Read allegedly called for Trump to be shot, writing, ‘Let’s shoot Trump honestly, where’s our shooter? I’m tired of living this money life.’
He allegedly continued in the comment thread by saying he had obtained ammunition and threatening to kill the president.
‘I just got a 308 and 305 round and I’m killing this pedo,’ Read wrote, according to prosecutors.
Investigators later found additional comments Read allegedly posted on October 17 beneath a separate KWCH 12 News report about Trump’s visit.
Read allegedly said he would shoot Trump himself, then claimed he knew where the president would speak and had already located nearby rooftops.

The posts led to a federal investigation and Read’s arrest in Clearwater on October 17.
He remains in federal custody pending a detention hearing.
Read is facing a federal charge of threatening the president, an offense punishable by up to five years in prison.
Ryan A Kriegshauser, the US attorney for Kansas, said the case underscored that political disagreements do not give anyone the right to issue threats of violence.
He added that Americans have the right to express forceful political views, but that freedom of speech has legal boundaries.
The Secret Service, US Marshals Service, Kansas Bureau of Investigation, Kansas Highway Patrol and Wichita Police Department are participating in the investigation.
Read allegedly said he would shoot the president himself (pictured boarding Air Force One before the rally), then claimed he knew where Trump would speak and had already identified nearby rooftops
Read’s reference to rooftops echoed the location used by Thomas Matthew Crooks when he shot Trump on July 13, 2024.
Crooks, a 20-year-old man from Bethel Park, Pennsylvania, fired eight rounds from an AR-15-style rifle at Trump just moments after he took the stage.
The president’s right ear was wounded, and a rally attendee, Corey Comperatore, died. Two others were injured.

sources.news_title: Man arrested for threats against Trump after commenting on 12 News social post
sources.text:
Man arrested for threats against Trump after commenting on 12 News social post
WICHITA, Kan. (KWCH) - A Clearwater man was arrested and charged with making threats against the president after replying to social media posts about Donald Trump’s visit to Park City.
The Kansas district of the U.S. Attorney’s Office filed a criminal complaint against 24-year-old Jaden Read, who made comments on a social media post from 12 News.
On Oct. 15, a Crime Stoppers tip led authorities to a Facebook post -- not one by 12 News -- on which Read made comments in response to an article detailing Trump’s visit to Heartland Credit Union Arena.
Read posted on Facebook, “Let’s shoot Trump honestly, where’s our shooter? I’m tired of living this money life.” Immediately after his first comment, Read posted a second comment on the same article, “I just got a 308 and a 305 round and I’m killing this pedo.”
Authorities found Read made two more threatening comments in response to a separate article from 12 News about Trump’s visit.
He commented, “Can we shoot him Kansas please I will myself.” A minute later, another comment from Read, “[I know] where your speech will be. Already mapped out roofs around. Finna get kirked [sic] since yall couldn’t help him.”
Read was arrested on Saturday in Clearwater and taken into federal custody. He’ll remain there until his detention hearing."

sources.news_title: Kansas Man Arrested For Allegedly Threatening Trump Before MAGA Rally in Wichita
Clearwater, Kansas, man arrested for online threats against President Trump
sources.text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. — A Clearwater, Kansas, man was arrested over the weekend for making online threats against President Donald Trump before his visit to Wichita.
The U.S. Attorney’s Office District of Kansas filed a criminal complaint on Saturday against Jaden J. Read, 24, for making threats against the president.
Read commented on several news station Facebook posts of articles sharing information about the president’s rally planned in support of Republican Sen. Roger Marshall, who faces Democrat Adam Hamilton in November.
The comments mentioned shooting the president, including Read saying, “… I will myself.”
Read also wrote that he knew where the speech would be given and he had “mapped out roofs around.”
He was taken into custody Saturday and will remain in federal custody until his detention hearing.
U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser says this is an example of how political violence and threats “will not be tolerated.”
“The First Amendment allows for robust disagreement but there are constraints. I caution people to stay within the bounds of constitutionally protected speech,” Kriegshauser said in a news release.
Trump's rally Monday evening is being held at the Heartland Credit Union Arena, which is located just north of Wichita in Park City, Kansas.
